## The question

> What actually happens after you click Sign Up?

**The walkaway:**

> Form checks, server checks, a password hash, then a session: the button is the last step.

## Script

| # | In | Type | s | Narration | Caption text (board) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0:00.0 | hook | 4.2 | That little Sign Up button can start a surprisingly long journey. | one click, a long way |
| 2 | 0:04.2 | hook | 3.6 | Your details shouldn't just land in a database unchecked. | not straight in |
| 3 | 0:08.8 | explain | 5.0 | First, the form checks basic things, like whether your email looks valid. | the form checks first |
| 4 | 0:13.8 | explain | 4.4 | Required fields have to be filled in, or the form stops. | empty means stopped |
| 5 | 0:17.2 | explain | 4.6 | Then your browser sends it to the website's server, over an encrypted connection. | over a sealed line |
| 6 | 0:22.8 | explain | 6.0 | The server checks again: is the request allowed, and does that email already have an account? | the server asks too |
| 7 | 0:28.8 | explain | 4.4 | Are the rules being followed? Only then is an account created. | rules, then the record |
| 8 | 0:32.2 | explain | 5.4 | A properly designed service stores a password hash, not your password in readable form. | a hash, not a password |
| 9 | 0:38.6 | explain | 4.8 | It may also create a session, so you stay signed in as you move around. | a key, not a password |
| 10 | 0:42.4 | myth-check | 5.8 | Here's the important bit: the button doesn't make an account secure. The checks and the password handling do. | button not security |
| 11 | 0:48.2 | recap | 4.4 | Validate. Protect. Store safely. | VALIDATE PROTECT STORE |
| 12 | 0:53.6 | outro | 3.4 | One click. Several safeguards. | WHAT SIGN UP REALLY DOES |

| 0109-c3 | 5 | HTTPS is HTTP carried over an encrypted connection, so the request travels sealed. | [HTTPS (MDN Glossary)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/HTTPS) | primary | 2026-10-31 |
